description: Hello. Tinkering with robotics at 7 sparked my builder mindset. Soon, I was coding in Scratch and C++, developing Roblox games and crafting hardware with Arduino & Raspberry Pi. My passion evolved into cybersecurity and systems: I earned my CEH credential, tackled CCNA training and even built a local network for peers. Now a part-time Network Engineer at Insight First running vMix broadcasts. I'm ready for the NASA Challenge to turn code, networks, and AI into tools for the space exploration.
summary: A sandbox junior astronaut misson trainer game that aims to teach students the real systems, engineering, as welll as the trade-offs of living in a space trough a cross-platform educational strategy simulator that is able to run on any Web Browser and a Electron Desktop App. It features a Mission Briefing and an Option to choose a landing site on the start menu, a 4 step interactive tutorial, a proggressive moon to mars campaign, and rotating daily missions that keeps the users engaged.
details:
Inside the game, a hour by hour simulation engine is intergrated to simulate NASA's Environmental Control, Life Support System and a In-Situ Resource Utilization conservation laws. The mechanics includes:

  • A resource system that players can manage which includes Power, Water, Wastewater, Oxygen, Carbon Dioxide, Hydroponic Food, Regolith, Spareparts which are 3D printed, and a Cryogenic Rocket Fuel that intergrates with one another.
  • A mechanic where when a Lunar Shadow Transit or Martian Dust Storm cuts solar output by 85%, players can throttle low-priority circuits using the Power Breaker Box (The options are: Off, 50%, or 100%) before the battery deplets and tripps llife support.
  • A mechanic where there is a time rewind and a logged decision that players use. When something terrible happens a player can easily rewind their progress, with an explanation of what the root problem or cause is in plain English, and highlight the exact problem and how to fix it.

This game is designed to engage players without overstimulating, using a UI inspired by the Cities Skyline game and utilizing a 2.5D isometric base so players can see visual cause and effect rather than overwhelming themselves. The game aims to teach real engineering trade-offs through play so players will discover why Mars's solar panel generates less than half the electricity of lunar panels and how hydrogen-rich waters, water walls, and baked regolith block solar protons. The game also preloads cached NASA data and includes several STEM guide quizzes that reward in-game science data. With the proton wrap push, this game will run 100% offline.

Through this game I hope that it bridges the gap between simplified games made for students or children and intimidating aerospace tool. Which hopefully inspired students to think like system engineers.

For building the game I leveraged Google's antigravity app a lot. Besides that I did use HTML, CSS, JavaScript for its frontend, and Node.js to utilize Electron. Note that I didn't publish the electron version of it. It's just for a pure concept instead of a live demonstration.
